llc.formation_doc: Articles of Organization (Form CD 030) with Transmittal Form 231
llc.formation_notes: $100 online; $110 by mail. Expedite: +$100 (2 business days), +$250 (same day). The SOS fee schedule (effective Sept 6, 2025) reportedly adds a $5 online service charge ($105 total), but sos.ga.gov was blocked (Cloudflare 403) today and could not be read.

annual_report.name: Annual Registration
annual_report.due: between January 1 and April 1 each year, starting the year after formation (2- or 3-year multi-year registration possible)
annual_report.late_penalty: $25 late fee if not filed/postmarked by April 1; extra $10 service charge for mail filing; risk of administrative dissolution

sources.title: Georgia.gov - Register an LLC with Georgia Secretary of State
sources.quote: Pay the $100 filing fee by approved credit card

sources.title: Georgia.gov - Renew an LLC
sources.quote: Your envelope must be postmarked by April 1 of the current year to avoid a $25 late fee.

sources.title: Georgia.gov blog - What Is An LLC? (2014)
sources.quote: Each LLC in Georgia is required to pay the $50 registration fee between January 1 and April 1

entity_level_taxes.name: Net worth tax (corporations, including S corporations)
entity_level_taxes.notes: Graduated net worth tax; corporations with net worth of $100,000 or less owe nothing but must file; maximum $5,000 for net worth over $22 million. Not applicable to LLCs taxed as partnerships/disregarded.

entity_level_taxes.name: Corporate income tax (only if S status not recognized for Georgia, or PTET election)
entity_level_taxes.notes: If S Corporation status is recognized for Georgia, shareholders pay the tax instead of the corporation

pte_elective_tax.rate_note: S corporations and partnerships may make an annual irrevocable election (HB 149, tax years from 2022) to pay tax at the entity level at the individual rate under O.C.G.A. 48-7-20(a.1): 4.99% for 2026 after HB 463.

sources.title: Georgia DOR - Corporate Income and Net Worth Tax
sources.quote: corporations with a net worth of $100,000 or less are not subject to tax but must file a return. The maximum is $5,000

sources.title: Georgia DOR - HB 149 Pass-Through Entity Tax FAQ
sources.quote: S Corporations and Partnerships may annually make an irrevocable election to pay income tax at the entity level.

personal_exemption.notes: No personal exemption for the taxpayer; dependent exemption raised from $4,000 to $5,000 per dependent for 2026 (HB 463). Standard deduction rises $375 (single) / $750 (MFJ) per year from 2027, up to $18,000 / $36,000, subject to delays.

income_tax_2026.surtaxes: None. HB 463 (signed May 11, 2026) cut the rate from 5.19% to 4.99% retroactive to Jan 1, 2026; further 0.125-point annual cuts from 2027 toward 3.99% subject to revenue triggers.

sources.title: HB 463 (as passed House and Senate), 2025-2026 session
sources.quote: the tax imposed pursuant to subsection (a) of this Code section shall be 5.19 percent 4.99 percent for taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2025 2026

sources.title: HB 463 - standard deduction
sources.quote: In the case of a married couple filing a joint return, $24,000.00 $30,000.00 ... single taxpayer ... $12,000.00 $15,000.00

sources.title: Governor's Office - Gov. Kemp signs legislation lowering taxes (May 11, 2026)
sources.quote: HB 463 lowers Georgia's state income tax rate from 5.19% to 4.99%, beginning January 1, 2026.

estimated_tax.required_if: expected gross income exceeds exemptions plus estimated deductions plus $1,000 of income not subject to withholding (2025 Form 500-ES wording)
estimated_tax.notes: Form 500-ES; later start dates if requirement first met after April 1

unemployment_2026.notes: GDOL FAQ: new employers assigned a total rate of 2.70% (FAQ may be dated; 2026 rate notices are in the Employer Portal). Wage base $9,500 since 2013.

notable: 2026 flat rate cut to 4.99% retroactively by HB 463 signed May 11, 2026, with standard deduction raised to $15,000 / $30,000 (https://gov.georgia.gov/press-releases/2026-05-11/gov-kemp-signs-legislation-lowering-taxes-and-supporting-economic-growth)
No franchise tax on LLCs; S corporations owe net worth tax only above $100,000 of net worth, capped at $5,000 (https://dor.georgia.gov/corporate-income-and-net-worth-tax)
PTET election available to S corps and partnerships at the individual rate (https://dor.georgia.gov/hb-149-pass-through-entity-tax-faq)
uncertain: sos.ga.gov (fee schedule, how-to guides) blocked by Cloudflare today. $100 formation fee read on georgia.gov; the $50 annual registration fee is from a 2014 georgia.gov blog post, not a 2026 SOS page. Possible $5 online / $10 mail service charges on top not verified.
New employer SUTA rate 2.70% is from a GDOL FAQ of unknown date; some sources cite 2.64%. Not verified for 2026.
2026 Form 500-ES not opened; threshold wording taken from the 2025 form.
